subject: Pricing inquiry: hosted API tool-calls + structured JSON metering
messages:
From: Jordan Levy <jordan.levy@aceroid.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ml-platform@aceroid.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: hosted API pricing for tool calls & JSON outputs

Hi Rachel,

Quick intro — I run platform procurement for Aceroid. We’re evaluating Redwood for our hosted inference tier and need a clear baseline to model costs for our product roadmap. Two specific asks:

1) How do you meter tool/function calls (when the model executes an external tool or a function/call) versus regular generation tokens? Is there a per-invocation surcharge in addition to token billing?

2) For structured output modes (JSON-only / schema-locked responses) does Redwood change metering — e.g., additional overhead for parsing/validation or different token accounting?

For context, our expected starter profile if we onboard would be roughly: 5M generated tokens/month, ~200k tool invocations (mostly short), and ~1k concurrent connections spread across multiple routes. We’ll also be evaluating options for committed spend and multi-month discounts.

Could you send a simple rate card for hosted API (per 1k tokens, per-invocation if any, any fixed fees) and a ballpark quote for the profile above, plus options for volume/commit discounts? If you can attach any example calculation sheets, that would be great — I’ll share them with engineering and procurement.

Thanks,
Jordan Levy
Platform Procurement
Aceroid

--
Attachment: example-invocation-log.csv (referenced)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Levy <jordan.levy@aceroid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: hosted API pricing for tool calls & JSON outputs

Jordan — thanks for the clear context. Short answers up front, followed by a spreadsheet and notes attached.

High level metering (hosted API, current public tier):
- Tokens: billed per 1k generated tokens by model family (we’ll attach the baseline rate card). Example baseline for the open-family models: $0.004 / 1k tokens generated.
- Tool/function invocations: charged as token usage + a small fixed invocation surcharge for bookkeeping and IO. Typical surcharge ranges from $0.0004 to $0.0008 per invocation depending on concurrency/throughput profile. The invocation itself also consumes tokens (request + response).
- Structured/JSON mode: token accounting does not change — payload tokens are billed the same as text. We do add a small structured-output overhead when schema enforcement/strict parsing is enabled (this is primarily CPU/validation time on our side) which is normally captured as a per-invocation processing fee (we’ve historically treated this in the same band as the function-call surcharge).

Ballpark for your profile (5M tokens + 200k invocations):
- Tokens: 5,000 * $0.004 = $20/month (that’s per 1k units -> 5,000 * 0.004) — example only using baseline model pricing.
- Invocation surcharge (assume $0.0006 per call): 200,000 * $0.0006 = $120
- Token usage for tool traffic (assume 1.5 tokens generated per invocation avg = 300k tokens -> 300 * $0.004 = $1.20)
- Estimated total monthly hosted bill (baseline, no discounts): ~$141.20

Notes: the above is illustrative and uses a low-cost baseline model. For production-quality LLMs (larger families / lower-latency paths) token rates and CPU surcharges will be higher. Also, when structured output is used with schema enforcement, we recommend adding a small buffer (~5-15%) in cost projections for retries and tooling overhead.

I’ve attached: Redwood_Baseline_RateCard_Q3.pdf and an ACEROID_RateCard_Q3.xlsx that contains a simple calculator you can drop your real usage into.

If you’re looking at a committed purchase, we can propose tiered discounts based on 12/24 month commitments and committed monthly spend. Ben — looping you and Laura for suggested discount bands and any SLO/contract questions.

Happy to run an actual cost-model from your logs if you can share a sample invocation trace (we can do this under an NDA if needed).

Best,
Rachel Kim

Jordan — thanks for the ask and thanks Rachel for the calc. Quick commercial note from my side:

We typically offer tiered discounts for committed hosted spend. For a 12-month commit we can be aggressive on invocation surcharges (we can waive/reduce the per-invocation fee at scale) and provide token discounts. Example starting offer:
- 12 month commit of $60k/month -> 20% off baseline token rates and 50% reduction in invocation surcharge (or invoice-credit arrangement).
- 24 month commit -> 25% token discount + up to 75% reduction in invocation surcharge and priority onboarding.

If your procurement needs a smaller starter, we can propose a pilot commit ($15k/month for 3 months) with a step-up clause to move into the 12-month band if metrics are met. We’ll need a basic SOW and SLOs to lock pricing (latency SLOs and uptime). Laura, can you confirm if the standard enterprise SOW + Redwood standard SLA fits here or need custom language?

Jordan, if you can confirm the target committed monthly spend band (pilot vs 12m vs 24m) I’ll draft a formal commercial term sheet and get legal looped. We’ll also include an explicit accounting line for structured-output processing so there are no surprises.

Thanks — Ben Carter
